text:
elaine: Quick share — ran an nsys capture against the KV-heavy workload and saw frequent kernel switches during the first ~300ms after request start. suspect warmup spikes + batching heuristics oscillating.

devin: ugh that sounds like the warmup window is too short so the runtime keeps reselecting small-kernel vs fused-kernel. did you capture nvtx brackets around batch boundaries?

elaine: yes, NVTX markers are there. timeline shows repeated pattern: small kernel (~0.8ms) -> giant kernel (~12ms) -> small kernel -> giant kernel, repeating for the first second. after ~1s it stabilizes to the giant kernel.

kevin: that pattern usually means the prefix/KV cache warmup is pushing sequence-length distribution out of the kernel selection heuristics. runtime picks the low-latency kernel initially, then sees longer sequences and switches. switching cost makes it noisy.

devin: capture flags i used: ```nsys profile --output=run1 -t cuda,nvtx,osrt --duration=10s --sample=cpu --force-overwrite``` but some of our earlier notes suggest using sampling + longer duration to cover warmup+steady state. also add `--capture-range=nvtx:bracket` to limit file size.

elaine: i tried `--duration=6s` earlier; file was tiny and missed the stabilization period. re-run with longer duration now. also noticed clock offset timestamps in the trace header, might be hiding sub-ms jitter.

kevin: two quick tips: 1) use `--trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt` to capture OS runtime markers for scheduling gaps, 2) set `--sample-interval=200us` (or smaller) so we don't alias short kernels. example CLI we recommend: ```nsys profile -o kvcache-warmup -t cuda,nvtx,osrt --duration=12s --sample-interval=200us --capture-range=nvtx:bracket```

devin: also add NVTX push/pop around the kv cache fill and batching decision points, e.g., ```nvtxRangePushA("kv_fill"); ... nvtxRangePop();``` helps correlate kernel timeline to logic.

elaine: ack. one more: `nsys stats` + `nsys-ui` show kernel timeline but i needed `nsys stats --report=overview` to get kernel runtime percent. saw 23% time spent on kernel switch overhead in the warmup window.

kevin: if you confirm, try a capture with synthetic warmup: preflight a few dummy requests to populate KV before main capture. that isolates whether kernel selection logic needs a warmup heuristic tweak vs a batching policy bug.

elaine: ran three quick experiments: 1) no warmup, 2) 5 warmup requests, 3) 20 warmup requests. results: no warmup -> noisy switching; 5 warmup -> reduced oscillation but still a couple switches; 20 warmup -> stable kernel selection from start. so it's clearly a cold-KV effect.

devin: nice repro. can you paste the small capture snippet of the kernel timeline (nsys shows kernel names + start/end) so i can check which kernels are being chosen?

elaine: pasted snippet: ```Kernel Name                Start (ms)  Duration (ms)
small_attention_kernel     12.34       0.78
large_fused_attention      13.25       11.9
small_attention_kernel     25.2        0.80
large_fused_attention      26.05       12.1```

kevin: confirms: small vs large. batching heuristics likely use observed sequence length percentiles; during KV fill sequence lengths fluctuate causing flip. i propose adding a sticky hysteresis to kernel selection (hold choice for N batches) or bias toward fused when bandwidth > threshold.

devin: agreement. for immediate mitigation we can bump KV prefetch + do a conservative kernel pin for dedicated nodes (force fused for first X tokens). long term: tweak heuristics.

elaine: i'll open a tiny RFC with the experiments + nsys captures attached. also logging the exact nsys CLI i used in case others run: ```nsys profile -o 1765001111-kv-warmup -t cuda,nvtx,osrt --duration=14s --sample-interval=200us --capture-range=nvtx:bracket --force-overwrite```

ops-bot: Run completed: uploaded capture to gs://redwood-nsys/1765001111-kv-warmup.qdrep (size: 285MB) :white_check_mark:

devin: thanks! i'll pull and add an annotation layer showing batch sizes over time and propose a hysteresis parameter. :thumbsup:

elaine: perfect. leaving notes in the RFC about clock-sync check — run `nsys profile --report=summary` and confirm system clocks are within 1ms, otherwise timeline alignment across hosts is sketchy.

kevin: one final note — when you re-run, try toggling `--capture-size` if file sizes are an issue, and avoid `--sample-interval` < 100us unless you need it; it balloons trace size.

elaine: got it. thanks everyone. i'll attach the three captures to the RFC and flag for perf-ops to consider sticky selection as a short-term flag toggle.
